prompt:
This is a bounded LTZZZ-owned public task under original task DEEP-SUPERAGENT-20261103. Context: the owner told the coordinator to run its own sweep, find engineering problems, hand them to the right team, and leave an audit trail. You have no network access and no file system, so the sweep observations were collected by the operator and are given below as a sanitized structural sample. You must NOT claim you ran any pipeline or read any repository.

OBSERVATIONS (last 40 pipeline runs plus backlog):
S01 same pipeline failed twice. cause: operator submitted three new queue cards in one push, then deleted two cards in a later push; the queue rejects both patterns by design. repeatable: false. blast: wasted two full runs, no code regression.
S02 build-and-publish pipeline failed once. cause: build step failure. repeatable: true. blast: published site not updated.
S03 service-observe run failed once. cause: probe step failure while the membership-free path was used. repeatable: unknown. blast: observation gap only, no write attempted.
S04 backlog: 30 pull requests open and unmerged, oldest well past review latency. cause: accumulation. repeatable: n/a. blast: review blindness, conflicts rising.
S05 test suite red on two assertions. cause: both assertions encode a payment contract that the owner already changed by decision; the tests were not updated to the new semantics. repeatable: true. blast: blocks any pipeline that runs the full suite.
S06 one active worker seat fails its upstream call on every batch while its peer seats succeed. cause: seat generation latency exceeding the fixed transport window. repeatable: true. blast: every batch is marked evidence-incomplete.
S07 planner rejects open-ended assigned tasks and returns an empty plan. cause: planner requires a checklist-shaped task. repeatable: true. blast: self-directed open work cannot be dispatched.

Task: for each of S01 to S07 give exactly one disposition from this fixed set: fix_now_by_operator, fix_now_by_engineering_seat, route_to_owner_decision, route_to_external_dependency, no_action_operator_error, drain_by_automation. Also give for each item the single field that best justifies your route, and never claim you fixed anything.

Rules you must apply and state:
1. a failure caused by operator misuse of a guarded interface is no_action_operator_error plus a note on the guard that caught it; it must not be counted as a code defect.
2. an assertion that encodes a superseded contract is not a product bug; routing it to engineering without the owner's decision would silently rewrite agreed semantics, so it must be route_to_owner_decision first.
3. an item whose cause sits outside this codebase must be route_to_external_dependency, never fix_now.
4. backlog drain by accumulation may be drain_by_automation only if no item needs a decision to merge; otherwise route_to_owner_decision.
5. nothing in this list authorises a merge, a deploy, a contract change or a payment change.

Then give: sweep_order (the sequence you would actually process these in, with the precedence rule), what_you_would_delegate (one line per item naming the seat you would hand it to and the acceptance check that seat must return), and audit_trail (what a third party could verify afterwards without trusting your statement).

Return concise JSON only: items (key, disposition, basis_field), sweep_order, precedence_rule, what_you_would_delegate, audit_trail, and a one-line honesty note. Fictional and structural only; preserve task and package IDs; do not repeat a provider request after an unknown result.
